clues: Before its commercial debut, this domestic machine appeared at the World Robot Conference and the World Manufacturing Convention.
It features a full-body motion system with 22 degrees of freedom, enabling it to perform expressive gestures and dance routines.
Using computer vision and voice recognition, it can identify household objects, discuss nearby items, and avoid dynamic obstacles.
Its long-term memory allows it to track family members' individual routines, retain conversational context, and issue reminders.
Its system breaks instructions into actionable steps and plans longer-term tasks rather than only responding to single prompts.
This companion humanoid was unveiled by Chery's robotics unit, AiMOGA, to adapt automotive manufacturing to domestic embodied AI.
